audit.whatIsWrong: content.early says 'Zac has no ranged poke and no pre-6 dash' and then names Elastic Slingshot in the same sentence. It also says 'his Q root comes online at level 3', and whys[2] repeats 'His Q root is online... deny his root cast distance'. Zac's Q is not a root and his E is a dash available from level 1.
audit.why: Stretching Strikes is an 800-range grab that throws you toward a second target he attacks — it displaces, it does not root. Elastic Slingshot is a dash, and it is a basic ability, so there is no 'pre-6' safety window at all. A Teemo told he is safe from dashes until 6 will stand at the wrong distance for five levels.
audit.corrected: Q Stretching Strikes is an 800-range grab-and-throw; E Elastic Slingshot is his dash and it exists from level 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer mentions that Zac's abilities cost health.
audit.why: Stretching Strikes, Unstable Matter and Elastic Slingshot are all paid for in percent of current health — he has no mana bar. Against a poison-poke laner that changes the entire trade calculus: every ability he answers you with adds to the damage your Toxic Shot is already doing, and a Zac who spams W to clear is doing your work for you.
audit.corrected: Q, W and E cost him a share of his current health — his own trade costs stack with your poison.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry tells you to shroom his blobs but never says what the passive actually does on death, or that it has a timer.
audit.why: Cell Division splits him into four bloblets on fatal damage and revives him from whichever survive, and it is on a five-minute cooldown. That single number decides whether a dive is worth committing to — and shrooms and Toxic Shot poison are unusually good at finishing bloblets.
audit.corrected: Cell Division's revive is a 5-minute cooldown; once it is spent he dies for real, and poison finishes bloblets.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's passive is called 'camouflage' in wants.you[2], whys[4] and content.late.
audit.why: Guerrilla Warfare grants Invisibility, not Camouflage — the wiki states he 'gains invisibility after 1.5 seconds without moving'. The two are different mechanics: camouflage is revealed by any nearby enemy, invisibility is not. Against a Zac who is walking down a side lane looking for you, that distinction is the whole reason the escape works.
audit.corrected: Guerrilla Warfare is Invisibility after 1.5s standing still — nearby enemies do not reveal it.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid gives Elastic Slingshot 'a long cooldown (around 20 seconds at early ranks)' and the full layer gives no number at all.
audit.why: It is 21/18/15/12/9 — genuinely long at rank 1 and genuinely short at rank 5, so 'around 20 seconds at early ranks' quietly stops being true exactly when he starts ranking it. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds, so your dart-per-slingshot ratio collapses from three to barely one across the lane.
audit.corrected: Elastic Slingshot 21s at rank 1 down to 9s at rank 5, against your flat 7s dart.

edits.before: A single Blinding Shot already shuts down Zac's autoattack trading before he can absorb a single blob — set the poke tone on wave one.
edits.after: A single Blinding Dart shuts down Zac's autoattack trading before he absorbs a blob, and every ability he answers with costs him health.

edits.before: Track Elastic Slingshot's cooldown and use camouflage passive to bait the cast, then punish the long lockout with a full poison-stack trade
edits.after: Track Elastic Slingshot at 21s on rank 1 and use Guerrilla Warfare invisibility to bait the cast, then punish the lockout with a poison trade

edits.before: Zac's level 1 is entirely autoattack-based — Blinding Shot negates it before a single blob even hits the floor.
edits.after: Zac's level 1 is entirely autoattack-based — Blinding Dart negates it before a single blob even hits the floor.

edits.before: His Q root is online but so is your full kit — step back to max Q range after the blind lands and deny his root cast distance.
edits.after: Stretching Strikes is a grab, not a root, and it costs him health — hold past its 800 units after the blind and it never starts.

edits.before: Let's Bounce is a teamfight tool, not a 1v1 tool — camouflage passive lets you vanish before he can commit, and shrooms cover his bounce-landing zones.
edits.after: Let's Bounce! is a teamfight tool, not a 1v1 tool — Guerrilla Warfare invisibility lets you vanish before he commits, and shrooms cover his landing zones.

edits.before: Zac has no ranged poke and no pre-6 dash — his only path to a trade is walking up and autoing or landing the telegraphed Elastic Slingshot wind-up. A single Blinding Shot erases his autoattack window entirely, so open every wave by walking up to Q range, dropping a blind, and then layering Toxic Shot autos as he retreats. Watch the ground for his Cell Division blobs: shroom those exact tiles immediately so he cannot run back and reabsorb the HP he just lost. His level 1 and 2 are among the weakest in the top lane — press that advantage hard before his Q root comes online at level 3.
edits.after: Zac has no ranged poke and no mana bar — Stretching Strikes, Unstable Matter and Elastic Slingshot are all paid for in his own current health, so every answer he gives you stacks with your poison. His trade options are walking up to auto, the 800-unit Q grab, or the telegraphed Elastic Slingshot wind-up, and that dash exists from level 1, not from 6. A single Blinding Dart erases the autoattack window, so open every wave by walking to Q range, blinding, and layering Toxic Shot as he retreats. Watch the ground for Cell Division blobs and shroom those exact tiles so he cannot reabsorb the HP he just spent.

edits.before: Elastic Slingshot is your one genuine danger — it has a visible wind-up animation and a long cooldown (around 20 seconds at early ranks). The moment you see him crouch into the cast, use Move Quick to dodge laterally; he cannot correct the trajectory. After he whiffs, his only follow-up is walking to you through mushrooms while blinded. With Q at max rank your blind window is long enough to auto-poke him down to blob-pickup range, then shroom the blobs so his passive sustain is gone. At level 6 his Let's Bounce does not meaningfully threaten a 1v1 — use the shroom net to hard-push the wave and rotate for dragon or deny his jungle with mushrooms at both entrances.
edits.after: Elastic Slingshot is your one genuine danger, and its cooldown is 21 seconds at rank 1 but only 9 at rank 5 — the free window you get early quietly disappears, so stop counting on it around the time he maxes it. The moment you see him crouch into the cast, use Move Quick to dodge laterally; he cannot correct the trajectory. After he whiffs, his only follow-up is walking to you through mushrooms while blinded. With Q at max rank your blind window is long enough to poke him to blob-pickup range, then shroom the blobs so his sustain is gone. Remember Cell Division's revive is a five-minute cooldown: once he has spent it, the next dive is real. At 6 Let's Bounce! does not meaningfully threaten a 1v1.

edits.before: - Zac Elastic Slingshot: matchup-defining — His engage. Blind + kite it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Zac Elastic Slingshot: 21s at rank 1 but 9s at rank 5 — his engage, and the early free window shrinks fast. - Stretching Strikes: 14s to 8s, an 800-unit grab. - Cell Division revive: 5 minutes. - Your dart: flat 7s.

edits.before: That is Zac's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Blobs are his sustain and his 5-minute revive — deny them and half his kit is gone.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Elastic Slingshot's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Trade around Elastic Slingshot: 21s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5, so the early window shrinks. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.

notes: Three separate mechanical errors in the content layer: Zac's Q was called a root (it is an 800-unit grab-and-throw), his E was described as arriving at 6 (it is a basic ability available from level 1, in a sentence that also names it), and Teemo's passive was called camouflage (the wiki says invisibility after 1.5s standing still — camouflage would be revealed by a nearby enemy, invisibility is not). Zac's health-cost resource and Cell Division's 5-minute revive timer were absent from both layers despite being the two facts that decide whether trades and dives are worth taking. Also note champ-data/_kits/teemo.json carries a 'knockup' kitFlag on Noxious Trap and _missing-interactions.json builds a 'knockup-enabler' headline for this matchup on top of it; the wiki lists Noxious Trap as slow-only with no displacement, so that flag is a false positive and nothing here relies on it.
